name: Capital One
description: Capital One is the largest issuer of credit cards in the US by outstanding balances (10-K, December 31, 2025), and it funds its lending mainly with insured deposits (its primary funding source per the 10-Q). Cardholders who carry balances pay interest (average yield 17.95 percent on card loans in 2025); merchants pay interchange and network fees whenever cards are used; and Capital One bears the credit losses when borrowers do not pay ($11.6 billion of card net charge-offs in 2025, a 5.09 percent rate). On May 18, 2025 it merged with Discover Financial Services for $51.8 billion, adding Discover's card loans and deposits and a payments-network business (the Discover Network, PULSE and Diners Club) that earns fees from other banks' cards; on April 7, 2026 it bought Brex, a corporate card and expense software company, for about $4.5 billion. Beyond cards it makes auto loans and commercial real estate and business loans. 74 percent of 2025 net revenue came from Credit Card, but only 31 percent of segment net income, because the provision for credit losses (9.1 billion in the segment) and higher expenses consumed most of it.

gics.note: Conventional filing only. Sector and sub-industry from Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30); no industry group or industry given there, so null. SEC SIC code is 6021 (National Commercial Banks) per EDGAR, so the SEC and GICS labels disagree: a bank charter but a card lender's economics.

hq.note: 1680 Capital One Drive, McLean, VA 22102 (SEC submissions record); bank holding company; principal operating subsidiary Capital One, National Association (CONA) (FY2025 10-K)

employees.note: Approximately 76,300 employees worldwide, called associates (FY2025 10-K human capital section). Includes the Discover workforce after the May 2025 merger.

businessLines.name: Credit Card
businessLines.shareBasis: Company-reported 74% of total net revenue in Table 7 of the FY2025 10-K (39,560 / 53,434 = 74.0%)
businessLines.how: Cardholders pay interest on balances they carry plus fees, and merchants pay interchange on every purchase; Capital One earns the spread over its funding cost and pays the losses when borrowers default, so profit swings with credit quality, loan growth and the allowance it sets aside for future losses.
businessLines.description: Domestic consumer card lending, personal loans (acquired with Discover), domestic small business card lending, and international card businesses in the UK and Canada.

revenue.note: Total net revenue; FY2024 $28,164M (+40%); FY2023 $25,669M. Net interest income $31,822M plus non-interest income $7,738M. Includes about 7.5 months of Discover after the 2025-05-18 merger.

businessLines.revenueNote: Total net revenue; FY2024 $28,164M (+40%); FY2023 $25,669M. Net interest income $31,822M plus non-interest income $7,738M. Includes about 7.5 months of Discover after the 2025-05-18 merger.

operatingProfit.note: Income from continuing operations before income taxes; net income from continuing operations $645M (31% of the segment total of $2,088M), down from $3,292M in FY2024 and $3,457M in FY2023. Provision for credit losses $19,066M (FY2024 $10,272M); non-interest expense $19,641M.

businessLines.marketShare: Largest US credit card issuer by outstanding credit card loan balance at 2025-12-31

businessLines.name: Consumer Banking
businessLines.how: Consumers and small businesses deposit money (insured deposits are the company's primary funding source), auto borrowers pay interest on loans, service charges and customer fees are collected, and network participants (primarily acquirers, merchants and issuers) pay fees for transactions on the Global Payment Network.
businessLines.description: Deposit gathering and lending for consumers and small businesses, national auto lending, and the services of the Global Payment Network (Discover Network, PULSE, Diners Club, Network Partners) added with Discover.

revenue.note: Total net revenue; FY2024 $8,718M (+20%); net interest income $8,758M plus non-interest income $1,675M (+141%, mostly from acquiring the Global Payment Network)

businessLines.revenueNote: Total net revenue; FY2024 $8,718M (+20%); net interest income $8,758M plus non-interest income $1,675M (+141%, mostly from acquiring the Global Payment Network)

operatingProfit.note: Income from continuing operations before income taxes; net income $1,225M (59% of segment total), down from $1,460M in FY2024 and $2,258M in FY2023; non-interest expense $7,524M includes Discover effects and a higher litigation accrual

businessLines.name: Commercial Banking
businessLines.how: Business borrowers pay interest on loans and fees for capital markets and treasury management services; commercial deposits fund lending; revenue is presented on a taxable-equivalent basis because some commercial investments earn tax credits.
businessLines.description: Lending, deposits, capital markets and treasury management for commercial real estate and commercial and industrial customers with annual revenues typically between $20 million and $2 billion. Brex (corporate cards and expense software, acquired April 7, 2026) is a business payments addition; the 10-Q read did not say which segment reports it.

revenue.note: Total net revenue (taxable-equivalent basis); FY2024 $3,601M; net interest income $2,334M plus non-interest income $1,321M

businessLines.revenueNote: Total net revenue (taxable-equivalent basis); FY2024 $3,601M; net interest income $2,334M plus non-interest income $1,321M

operatingProfit.note: Income from continuing operations before income taxes; net income $1,043M (50% of segment total), down from $1,209M in FY2024

businessLines.name: Other (corporate treasury and unallocated)
businessLines.how: Not a client business; it carries treasury and corporate items that the three segments are not held responsible for.
businessLines.description: Corporate investment portfolio and asset and liability management by Corporate Treasury, unallocated corporate expenses and residual tax items.

operatingProfit.note: Net loss from continuing operations after tax; FY2024 -$1,214M; company-reported -40% of the segment total
